rounds.title: Swift foundations and ownership
rounds.brief: Explain syntax and semantics clearly before introducing production architecture.
steps: Spend five minutes outlining the value, error and ownership mental model.
Answer the six prompts without revealing model answers; ask for missing assumptions.
Use the remaining time to change one input and debrief the mistaken predictions.
evidence: Correct assignment and optional/error distinctions.
An ownership graph rather than only weak-self vocabulary.
One runnable or clearly labeled predicted example, plus a next retrieval task.

rounds.title: UI implementation and lifecycle review
rounds.brief: Defend a screen under changing content, ownership and layout conditions.
steps: Spend five minutes defining the screen's visible behavior and state owner.
Discuss lifecycle, stable identity, layout and editing using the selected prompts.
Finish with large-text, RTL, keyboard, reuse and interrupted-navigation evidence.
evidence: No conflation of SwiftUI identity and UIKit controller lifetime.
A stable-item and obsolete-result policy.
Specific device/interaction gaps and a bounded verification matrix.

rounds.title: Concurrency, streams and account-scoped data
rounds.brief: Reason about asynchronous interleavings instead of reciting API names.
steps: Draw the owners of UI, shared work and final durable commit.
Answer each prompt with a controlled completion ordering.
Debrief cancellation, error preservation and A-to-B-to-A account transitions.
evidence: Distinguishes suspension, isolation, reentrancy and background work.
A precise buffer, cancellation and shared-operation contract.
Deterministic fake gates and separate cache versus UI publication checks.

rounds.title: Performance investigation and optimization defense
rounds.brief: Propose an optimization only after establishing correctness and a measurement contract.
steps: Define operation, denominator, baseline, target device and observation conditions.
Trace startup, frame, memory and resource hypotheses with the selected prompts.
Conclude with raw evidence requirements, regression gates and residual uncertainty.
evidence: No invented p95, energy gain or physical-device result.
Separates mechanism evidence from outcome measurements.
Tradeoffs preserve product behavior and identify conditions that reverse the recommendation.

rounds.title: Build variants, libraries and delivery contracts
rounds.brief: Explain the installed artifact and its dependency/resource graph.
steps: Map target, scheme, configuration, environment and bundle identity.
Review dependency, generated code, resources and verification coordinates.
Rehearse reconstruction and installed-client recovery without performing a release.
evidence: Package/product/target/import and requirement/pin distinctions.
Effective setting and target-membership evidence.
A narrow verification matrix and an honest recovery boundary.

rounds.title: Platform services and cross-process boundaries
rounds.brief: Keep trust, permission, scene, process and durable-state ownership explicit.
steps: Define a synthetic workflow that spans route, login, cache and system surfaces.
Release delayed events after changing account, document, scene or process conditions.
Debrief device, signing, interprocess and protected-data checks that remain pending.
evidence: No promise of exact background or widget scheduling.
Typed failure and stale-owner handling at the final transaction.
Distinct source, fake, device and distribution evidence.

rounds.title: Staff-level design, migration and influence
rounds.brief: Practice an architectural decision under constraints, not a memorized system-design script.
steps: Spend ten minutes defining users, constraints, success criteria and decision ownership.
Compare at least two alternatives and an incremental compatibility seam.
Address measurement, privacy, rollout, recovery and cross-team verification.
Use the debrief to state what evidence would reverse the recommendation.
evidence: A bounded proposal with alternatives and measurable acceptance.
Explicit risk owners, compatibility stages and recovery constraints.
Reproducible reviewer evidence and communication, not a claim that a score confers staff readiness.

rounds.title: Android-to-iOS engineering handoff
rounds.brief: Share a product contract across platforms without pretending their implementations are identical.
steps: Identify the shared product invariants and platform-specific owners.
Translate one Android assumption and demonstrate where it fails on iOS.
Finish with a reviewable implementation/verification handoff and residual specialist gaps.
evidence: Precise Kotlin/Java analogy boundaries.
Independent lifecycle, executor, resource and platform-availability reasoning.
An actionable evidence ledger that another engineer could reproduce.
